canonical_example.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:


$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-z &=1 \\ 2x+y+3z &=4 \\ 5x+4y+z &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$


Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is


$$
M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 4 & 1 & 7\end{array} \right].
$$



Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 4 & 1 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 2 \\ 5 & 4 & 1 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now


$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3 \\ y &=-2 \\ z &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$



So, we have the solution $x=3,$ $y=-2,$ and $z=0.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle 3,-2,0 \rangle.$
